chunks: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'By God! If I owned anything from the affairs of the people, I would straighten them by the sword and the whip until they would be divorcing according to the waiting period, just as God, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded.'

key_terms.بِالسَّيْفِ وَالسَّوْطِ: The sword and whip are instruments of enforcement under Islamic governance; their mention here underscores the Imam's view that this ruling requires coercive enforcement due to widespread non-compliance.
key_terms.لِلْعِدَّةِ: The 'iddah is the prescribed waiting period a woman must observe after divorce before she can remarry. Divorce pronounced outside the 'iddah conditions (i.e., not during a period of purity from menstruation) is considered invalid in Shia jurisprudence.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about enforcing divorce according to the waiting period?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) expresses intense frustration over widespread neglect of the divinely prescribed rules of divorce, particularly the obligation to divorce according to the 'iddah (waiting period) as mandated in Surah al-Talaq. Speaking to his companion Abu Baseer, the Imam invokes an oath by God and employs hyperbolic language — the sword and whip — to emphasize the gravity of this neglect and the severity of the divine command being flouted. This statement reflects both the Imam's deep commitment to implementing divine law and his recognition that during his time, political authority to enforce such rulings was beyond his reach.
